evals.prompt: I want to try Spider Silk for a tiny side project. Set up a fresh Gradle project in ./decks-api with a Main class that serves GET /api/decks as a JSON array of decks (id and name, just hardcode two of them) and GET /health. Keep it minimal, Java 21.
evals.expected_output: A Gradle build depending on net.benelog.spidersilk:spider-silk-core from Maven Central, and a Main that registers both routes with lambdas and writes the JSON through the framework's own Json API or a JsonWriter, with no reflective JSON library.
expectations: build.gradle declares mavenCentral() in repositories
build.gradle depends on net.benelog.spidersilk:spider-silk-core
No dependency on Jackson, Gson, or another reflective JSON library is added
Routes are registered with app.get(...) lambdas, not annotations
The decks JSON is built with Json.object()/Json.array() or a JsonWriter and returned through WebResponse.json(...)
No call to the removed Json.obj() or Json.arr() appears
The server is started with app.start(...)

evals.prompt: In our spider-silk app (DeckRoutes.java registers everything on `app`), add GET /api/decks/{deckId} and POST /api/decks. The id is a number and a non-numeric id should come back as 400, not 500. POST takes {"name": "..."} and should answer 201 with the created deck. DeckService already has find(long) and create(String).
evals.expected_output: Handlers that read the id with pathParamLong, parse the body with req.bodyJson(reader) through a hand-written JsonReader, and answer the POST with .status(HttpStatus.CREATED).
expectations: The id is read with req.pathParamLong("deckId") (or pathParam with a parser), not Long.parseLong on pathParam with a manual try/catch
The POST body is read with req.bodyJson(...) and a hand-written JsonReader, or req.bodyJson() with getString
The POST answers with .status(HttpStatus.CREATED)
No reflective binding such as bodyAsClass or ObjectMapper.readValue is used
Handlers return a WebResponse rather than writing to a context object

evals.prompt: add login to my spider silk app: POST /login checks the password with UserService.authenticate(name, pw) and remembers the user, everything under /admin must redirect to /login when nobody is logged in, and POST /logout ends the session. users are a User record.
evals.expected_output: Session writes and reads through req.session() (set, get with User.class, invalidate), and a beforeRoute or beforeRequest filter on /admin/* that returns a redirect or null.
expectations: The login stores the user with req.session().set("user", user) or an equivalent key
The guard reads the user with req.session().get(key, User.class) or req.session().get(key)
Logout calls req.session().invalidate()
The removed methods sessionAttr, setSessionAttr, removeSessionAttr, and invalidateSession do not appear
The /admin guard is registered as beforeRoute("/admin/*", ...) or beforeRequest("/admin/*", ...) with the trailing *
The guard returns WebResponse.redirect("/login") when nobody is logged in and null otherwise

evals.prompt: Every response from our Spider Silk service needs an X-Request-Id header, including 404s, error pages, and static files. I tried app.afterRoute((req, res) -> res.header("X-Request-Id", id())) but the 404s don't have it. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The header moves to app.responseFilter(...), with the reason that an after-filter only sees routes that returned normally.
expectations: The fix registers the header with app.responseFilter((req, res) -> ...)
The filter returns the response with the header added rather than discarding the result of res.header(...)
The explanation says an afterRoute filter does not run for 404s, error responses, or static files

evals.prompt: Our spider-silk app shows the default plain-text 404. I want a styled not-found page using our jte template at src/main/resources/jte/not-found.jte that gets the requested path. Also make any uncaught 500 show jte/oops.jte.
evals.expected_output: Two statusPage registrations rendering templates by name without the .jte extension.
expectations: The 404 page is registered with app.statusPage(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, ...)
The 500 page is registered with app.statusPage(HttpStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, ...)
The removed app.error(...) method is not used
Templates are named "not-found" and "oops" without the .jte extension
The requested path is passed to the template model from req.path()

evals.prompt: Ops says our servers must run Tomcat, not Jetty. We use Spider Silk 1.1.0 with Gradle. What do I change so the same App runs on embedded Tomcat? Don't pull in anything we don't need.
evals.expected_output: Add spider-silk-tomcat, optionally exclude the Jetty group, and set app.server((app, port) -> new TomcatServer(app).port(port)).
expectations: The answer adds net.benelog.spidersilk:spider-silk-tomcat as a dependency
The answer wires it with app.server((app, port) -> new TomcatServer(app).port(port)) or an equivalent WebServerFactory
The answer mentions the optional exclude of group org.eclipse.jetty.ee10
The answer does not add spider-silk-undertow or any template extension module
The routes and handlers are left unchanged

evals.prompt: Write tests for the POST /api/decks endpoint in our spider-silk project: one end-to-end test through HTTP and one that calls DeckController.createDeck directly. We use JUnit 5 and AssertJ. No Spring in this project.
evals.expected_output: An end-to-end test with WebTest.test(app, client -> ...) and a unit test built from TestRequest, both from spider-silk-test, with no mock library.
expectations: The test dependency net.benelog.spidersilk:spider-silk-test is used (testImplementation or test scope)
The end-to-end test uses WebTest.test(app, client -> ...)
The unit test builds the request with TestRequest.post("/api/decks") and a jsonBody(...) or body(...)
No Mockito, MockMvc, or MockHttpServletRequest is used
The unit test asserts on the returned WebResponse, such as its status()

evals.prompt: GET /api/cards in my spider silk app should accept ?page= (default 1), ?size= (default 20), and an optional ?q= search term. If q is missing just list everything. I wrote req.param("q", null) and it doesn't compile??
evals.expected_output: Defaults through paramLong(name, default) or param(name, Integer::parseInt, default), and the optional string through paramOrNull("q"), with the reason the null default does not compile.
expectations: The page and size are read with a default, such as req.paramLong("page", 1) or req.param("page", Integer::parseInt, 1)
The optional search term is read with req.paramOrNull("q") or req.queryParamOrNull("q")
The explanation says param(name, null) is ambiguous between the default and the parser overloads
A present but non-numeric page is left to answer 400, not silently replaced by the default

evals.prompt: After upgrading our Spider Silk app to 1.2.0 these lines stopped compiling: `WebResponse.json("{\"status\":\"up\"}")`, `Json.obj().put("n", 1)`, `app.error(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, h)`, `completion.failure()`, and `for (Guard g : app.guards())`. What are the new names?
evals.expected_output: rawJson(String), Json.object(), statusPage(...), writeFailure(), and Hook/hooks(), each with the reason it was renamed or a pointer to it.
expectations: WebResponse.json(String) is replaced with WebResponse.rawJson(String)
Json.obj() is replaced with Json.object()
app.error(status, handler) is replaced with app.statusPage(status, handler)
completion.failure() is replaced with completion.writeFailure()
Guard and guards() are replaced with Hook and app.hooks()

evals.prompt: Our export endpoint GET /api/cards/export builds a List of 500k cards and returns WebResponse.json(cards, CARDS) and the heap blows up. How do I stream it with spider silk? CardService has eachCard(Consumer<Card>). Clients can take either a JSON array or NDJSON.
evals.expected_output: WebResponse.jsonArray(sink -> ...) or WebResponse.ndjson(sink -> ...) writing one card at a time from eachCard, with the caveat that a failure after commitment cannot change the status.
expectations: The answer uses WebResponse.jsonArray(sink -> ...) or WebResponse.ndjson(sink -> ...)
Cards are written one at a time with sink.write(card, writer) inside cardService.eachCard(...)
No full List of cards is built before responding
The answer notes that once streaming has started a failure cannot change the status code

evals.prompt: Security review question for our spider-silk service: which filters cover /admin paths, and do any status pages exist? I don't want to read all of Routes.java. Can the app print that at startup?
evals.expected_output: Iterate app.hooks() with a switch over the sealed Hook records, and app.routes() for the routes, printed after registration.
expectations: The answer reads the registrations through app.hooks()
It pattern-matches the sealed Hook records such as Hook.BeforeRoute, Hook.BeforeRequest, and Hook.StatusPage
It uses app.routes() for the routes themselves
No reflection or classpath scanning is proposed

evals.prompt: I need a /files/{something} route in my spider silk app that serves anything under /srv/shared, including nested folders like /files/2024/reports/q1.pdf. Missing files should be a 404 not a 500.
evals.expected_output: A /files/{path*} route reading req.pathParam("path"), resolving it under the root with a traversal check, and throwing HttpException(NOT_FOUND) for a missing file before WebResponse.file(path).
expectations: The route pattern uses a named tail variable such as /files/{path*}
The remainder is read with req.pathParam("path")
A missing or non-regular file answers 404 through HttpException(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND, ...) or WebResponse.empty(HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND)
The resolved path is checked to stay under /srv/shared
The file is served with WebResponse.file(path), or StaticFiles.directory(...) is proposed as the alternative
